messages:
maria: heads up — after the CMK rotation last night (us-east-1) our cross-account analytics job in acct 222222222 started failing on kms:Decrypt. error: "AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/analytics-consumer/session123 is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource"

sanjay: are these jobs assuming a role in account 111111111111 or in 222222222? quick note: the arn you pasted looks like an assumed-role in 111111111111 (so the service doing the decrypt is running in acct 111...), but the key is in acct 222.

jules: can you paste the key policy and the exact error from cloudtrail? sometimes rotation surfaces policies that were implicitly matching the old flow.

maria: cloudtrail entry: 
```
{
  "eventTime": "2026-03-07T04:12:05Z",
  "eventName": "Decrypt",
  "userIdentity": {
    "type": "AssumedRole",
    "arn": "arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/analytics-consumer/session123"
  },
  "errorMessage": "User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222222:key/abcd-ef01"
}
```

maria: key policy attached (redacted): 
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "EnableAccountAccess",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:root"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowSomeRole",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/analytics-consumer"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

leo: aha — that key policy allows the role ARN, but the request is coming from the assumed-role principal (sts assumed-role ARN). normally allowing the role arn should be sufficient, but if you used any aws:PrincipalArn conditions or if the rotation changed the principal mapping (or session name expectations), it can fail. Also double-check whether the rotate job re-created the key as a new alias/key-id vs rotating the key material — if it created a new CMK, old grants/policies might not have been copied.

sanjay: two quick fixes: 1) update the key policy to allow the assumed-role principal pattern via condition, e.g.: 
```json
"Condition": {
  "StringLike": {"aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/analytics-consumer/*"}
}
```
2) create an explicit grant for the consumer role (grants survive rotation of key material but not if the key was replaced): 
```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/our-service-key --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/analytics-consumer --operations Decrypt GenerateDataKey --name crossacct-analytics-grant
```

jules: small caveat — if your app uses envelope encryption properly, in most flows you need kms:GenerateDataKey for encrypt, then kms:Decrypt for re-opening. If the job only calls Decrypt (e.g., re-encrypt path), ensure both ops are allowed. Also if the decrypt is triggered through another AWS service (S3, EBS), you might need kms:ViaService or Service principal entries in the key policy.

maria: we definitely use GenerateDataKey in the producer path. consumer just calls Decrypt on the encrypted data key. key rotation job was the managed rotation (EnableKeyRotation) not a key replacement. so I think grants/policies should've remained. weird.

leo: can you check whether the key policy had any Condition on aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn? sometimes people harden policies to specific session names or source arns which break assumed-role sessions with different session names after rotation tests.

maria: policy fragment we had originally (before rotation) had no conditions. after rotation job, nothing in policy changed per the console.

sanjay: run AWS CLI to list grants for the key: 
```bash
aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222222:key/abcd-ef01
```
If there are no grants for the consumer, create one. if there are grants but granteePrincipal is an IAM user that no longer exists, delete and recreate.

maria: ran list-grants — empty. guessing our previous setup relied purely on key policy allow for role arn. i'll try the grant now.

ops-bot: rotation/2026-03-06T23:58:12Z completed for key/abcd-ef01 (managed rotation) :information_source:

maria: created a grant with the CLI (used the example above). immediately retried the analytics job and it succeeded. :tada:

jules: nice. follow-up: we should add a smoke test in the rotation runbook that validates cross-account decrypts (run a GenerateDataKey/Encrypt/Decrypt between accounts) and if no grants exist, fail rotation or create grants via automation.

sanjay: agree — also add a step to the rotation playbook: verify alias still points to the same key-id (managed rotation shouldn't change id, but our provisioning has had bugs). if rotation replaced the key (new key-id) you must replicate policies/grants.

maria: created an issue in infra repo and added the smoke test task. thanks all. :heart: 

leo: TL;DR: common causes for AccessDenied after rotation: key replaced vs rotated, key policy conditions that match assumed-role ARNs incorrectly, missing kms:GenerateDataKey permission, or absent grants for cross-account roles. fix was to create a KMS grant for the consumer role or broaden key policy to match assumed-role session ARNs."
